answer: Agents could require each newcomer to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before earning reputation-weighted trades. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply the locked value: each account needs its own deposit, and a detected fraud can forfeit it. This makes a sybil campaign costly in capital and time, while honest newcomers can wander the tundra of early exchanges without buying trust outright; pigment in a profile or a new name cannot substitute for collateral.
